title: SIU clears officer in fatal shooting; Weapon inadvertently discharged during struggle killing addict in pharmacy break-in, director rules
article: A Toronto police officer has been cleared of wrongdoing forhis role in a fatal shooting in a Roncesvalles pharmacy, the province's Special Investigations Unit has ruled.
The officer's weapon inadvertently discharged during a struggle with 42-year-old David Fetterly, a drug addict, who had broken into the Solarski Pharmacy wearing a balaclava.

"In my view there are no reasonable grounds to believe that the subject officer committed any criminal offence," ruled SIU director Ian Scott, in one of his first decisions since assuming the post last month.

On March 8, the officer was patrolling the Parkdale area, at Roncesvalles and Garden Aves., around 3 50 a.m. when he heard an alarm. The officer noticed the front door to a local pharmacy had been pried open. Fetterly was inside. The officer ordered him to surrender, but Fetterly refused. The officer struck him with a baton, but it had little effect, the SIU said in a statement.

"Mr. Fetterly resisted and attempted to evade arrest by moving quickly to the front door where he turned around and grabbed the officer's wrist," Scott said in the ruling. "The officer ... responded by pulling and twisting his arm in an attempt to break Mr. Fetterly's hold. Unfortunately, the officer's firearm discharged unintentionally."
Fetterly was hit by a single bullet to the right side of his back. He managed to walk outside and collapsed on the sidewalk. The officer performed CPR, but Fetterly was pronounced dead in hospital.

Fetterly was the uncle of slain Hamilton teen Chantele Fetterly. The 16-year-old's ex-boyfriend stabbed her in the heart with a kitchen knife. This past July, just a few days after the one-year anniversary of her death, the boy, now 17, was sentenced to 21/2 years in prison, in addition to the year he was in custody prior to the trial.
"It's hard to keep going," said Sandra Fetterly-Brown, Chantele's mother and Fetterly's sister. "First Chantele. Then David ... I can't even believe this has happened to our family."
Fetterly-Brown said her brother had a history of mental illness and suffered from addiction. He was also one of her best friends, she said.
